mainTopic: Knives and skewers on יום טוב, מכשירי אוכל נפש, רב מלכיו versus רב מלכיא, and buying meat from a butcher on יום טוב
overview: The amud opens by finishing two stories in which a student saw his teacher quietly sharpen a knife on יום טוב while saying he was only removing fat. This shows the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, but it is הלכה ואין מורין כן. The גמרא then asks whether one may show a שחיטה knife to a חכם on יום טוב and brings three views, and רב יוסף allows sharpening a dull knife that still cuts with difficulty. A nicked knife, a crushed skewer, and sweeping an oven all depend on the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן about מכשירי אוכל נפש. The גמרא explains each side from the פסוק "הוא לבדו יעשה לכם". שמואל then forbids straightening a bent skewer and moving a used skewer, and other אמוראים discuss when it may be put in a corner. A side discussion sorts out which rulings belong to רב מלכיו and which to רב מלכיא. Finally a new משנה forbids naming a price to a butcher on יום טוב, and the גמרא's explanation of how to get meat continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The teacher who hid his sharpening
steps.stepSummary: Continuing a story earlier, a student saw his teacher running a knife over a basket's rim on יום טוב. The teacher said he was removing fat, but the student understood he was sharpening it. The teacher held the הלכה permits it but did not want to teach it publicly.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He was] running the knife over the rim of a basket. I asked him: Is the Master doing this to sharpen it, or to remove its fat? He told me: To remove its fat. But I understood his real intention, that he was doing it to sharpen it. He held: This is the הלכה, but we do not publicly rule that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that started earlier, showing what a great teacher actually did with his knife on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teacher's action showed he agreed with רבי יהודה that sharpening is allowed. But he gave a different reason out loud, because the rule is הלכה ואין מורין כן: true הלכה, yet not announced to the public so people will not take it too far.

keyTerms.meaning: its fat (the grease stuck on the knife)
a basket made of palm branches
it is the הלכה, but we do not publicly rule this way

steps.confusionAlert: The teacher was not lying about the הלכה. He really held it was permitted. He only hid it so the public would not hear an open ruling to sharpen knives on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the category הלכה ואין מורין כן: a permitted practice that a רב may follow and quietly allow, but must not announce publicly.

phrases.english: running the knife over the rim of a basket,
phrases.notes: The beginning of this story (who said it and before whom) is earlier.

phrases.english: and I said to him:
Is the Master doing this to sharpen it,
or to remove its fat?
And he said to me: To remove its fat.
But I saw from his intention that he was doing it to sharpen it,
and he holds: It is the halacha, but we do not rule this way publicly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story earlier that supports the ruling like רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי יהודה (sharpening permitted) but is not publicly taught.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teacher's actual behavior, sharpening a knife on a basket rim on יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי sees רבה do the same thing
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells a matching story: his teacher רבה ran a knife over the edge of a millstone on יום טוב. He said it was to remove fat, but אביי understood he was sharpening it, because the הלכה permits it but is not taught publicly.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I was standing before my Master, and he was running a knife over the edge of a millstone. I asked him: Does the Master want to sharpen it, or to remove its fat? He told me: To remove its fat. But I understood his real intention, that he was sharpening it. He held: This is the הלכה, but we do not publicly rule that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, almost identical story, this time told by אביי about his teacher רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second story strengthens the first: two different great teachers both quietly sharpened knives. This confirms that the הלכה really follows רבי יהודה, while the policy of not ruling it publicly stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: I was standing before my Master

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories teach one idea: sharpening a knife on יום טוב is really allowed (like רבי יהודה), but it is הלכה ואין מורין כן, so the teachers hid their real reason.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
I was standing before my Master,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲוָה קָא מְעַבַּר סַכִּינָא אַשִּׂפְתָּא דְרִחְיָא.
phrases.english: and he was running a knife over the edge of a millstone.
And I said to him:
Does the Master want to sharpen it,
or to remove its fat?
And he said to me: To remove its fat.
But I saw from his intention that he was doing it to sharpen it,
and he holds: It is the halacha, but we do not rule this way publicly.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story confirming the same point as step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי יהודה but is not publicly taught.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's behavior as reported by אביי.

steps.title: May one show a knife to a חכם on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new question: on יום טוב, may a person bring a slaughtering knife to a חכם so he can check it for nicks?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked among them: What is the law about showing a knife to a חכם on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question connected to knives on יום טוב. This sets up the opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שחיטה, a knife must be checked for nicks. The worry is that bringing knives to a חכם for checking looks like an ordinary weekday activity, which might not fit the honor of יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised among them
to show a knife to a sage (so he checks it)

phrases.english: A question was raised among them:

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לְהַרְאוֹת סַכִּין לְחָכָם בְּיוֹם טוֹב?
phrases.english: What is the law about showing a knife to a sage on a Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְהַרְאוֹת סַכִּין לְחָכָם בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from sharpening a knife to checking a knife on יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether bringing a שחיטה knife to a חכם for inspection is allowed on יום טוב.

steps.title: One חכם permits, the רבנן forbid
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב ביזנא allows showing the knife to a חכם on יום טוב, but the רבנן forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי the son of רב ביזנא permitted it, and the רבנן forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first two answers to the question: one permits and one forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרי sees checking a knife as a needed preparation for food, so it is allowed. The רבנן forbid it because people lining up with knives for a חכם looks like a weekday activity.

keyTerms.meaning: רב מרי, son of רב ביזנא

phrases.aramaic: רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב בִּיזְנָא שָׁרֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Rav Bizna, permitted it,
and the Rabbis forbade it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב בִּיזְנָא שָׁרֵי, וְרַבָּנַן אָסְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 with a dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dispute: רב מרי permits, the רבנן forbid.

steps.title: רב יוסף's middle path: the scholar checks privately
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says a תלמיד חכם may check his own knife privately and then lend it to others to use.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: A תלמיד חכם checks it for himself, and lends it to others.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a third, in-between answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem of the רבנן was the public weekday look of bringing knives to a חכם. If the חכם checks his own knife at home and then lends it out, nobody sees a public inspection, yet people still get a properly checked knife.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views on showing a knife to a חכם on יום טוב: רב מרי permits, the רבנן forbid, and רב יוסף says the חכם checks his own knife privately and lends it out.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
A Torah scholar checks it for himself,
and lends it to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רוֹאֶה לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a compromise between the two opinions in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Private checking by the scholar is allowed, and the knife may then be lent to others.

steps.title: A dulled knife may be sharpened on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a knife that has become dull may be sharpened on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: A knife that became dull may be sharpened on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new ruling about sharpening a knife that has gone dull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knife that is only dull (not nicked) is still a working tool. Sharpening it just improves it for cooking and שחיטה, so it is permitted on יום טוב.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
A knife that became dull —
it is permitted to sharpen it on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by the same רב יוסף, returning to the topic of sharpening.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knife that became dull may be sharpened on יום טוב.

steps.title: Only if the knife still cuts with difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The permission to sharpen a dull knife applies only when it still cuts, even with effort.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only when it still cuts, though with difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב יוסף's ruling to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the knife still cuts with difficulty, sharpening it only improves an existing tool. If it cannot cut at all, sharpening it is like making a new tool, which is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think every dull knife may be sharpened. If it no longer cuts at all, sharpening it is forbidden, because that is like making a new tool.
steps.whatToRemember: A dull knife may be sharpened on יום טוב only if it still cuts with difficulty. This counts as improving a tool, not making a new one.

phrases.english: And this applies only
when it still cuts, though with difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי הוּא דְּפָסְקָא אַגַּב דּוּחְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 6 to a knife that still cuts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sharpening is permitted only when the knife still cuts with difficulty. Otherwise it is like making a new tool.

steps.title: Nicked knife, crushed skewer, and oven sweeping all depend on one dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא (or רב יוסף) teaches that fixing a nicked knife, a crushed skewer, or sweeping an oven and stove on יום טוב all depend on the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא taught, and some say it was רב יוסף: a knife that got nicked, a skewer that got crushed, and sweeping out an oven or stove on יום טוב are all cases where we have arrived at the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: A teacher groups three cases together and says that one known dispute decides all of them. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא quotes that dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these three actions is cooking itself. Each one gets a tool or appliance ready so that cooking can happen. That shared feature is why all three fall into the same disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (it was a different speaker)
Crushed or bent (its point broke off)
Sweeping the coals out of an oven and a stove

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב חִסְדָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda taught, and some say it was Rav Yosef:
Both a knife that became nicked,
and a skewer that was crushed,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד גְּרִיפַת תַּנּוּר וְכִירַיִם בְּיוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: and sweeping an oven and stove on a Festival —
we have arrived at the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: Their law depends on this dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the knife-sharpening discussion into a general category of fixing tools on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fixing a nicked knife, a crushed skewer, or sweeping an oven on יום טוב depends on the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא: food preparation only, or also its preparatory steps
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is אוכל נפש. רבי יהודה also permits מכשירי אוכל נפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is food preparation. רבי יהודה permits even the things that make food preparation possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that contains the dispute mentioned in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, only work done to the food itself is allowed on יום טוב. רבי יהודה also allows work on the tools that make cooking possible, such as fixing a knife. Our three cases are exactly these kinds of preparatory steps.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Preparing food to eat (the work permitted on יום טוב)
Preparatory steps that make food preparation possible (for example, fixing tools)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse אוכל נפש, which is work on the food itself, with מכשירי אוכל נפש, which is work on the tools used for food. The whole dispute is about the second category.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: As it is taught: there is no difference between a Festival and Shabbat
except food preparation alone.
Rabbi Yehuda permits
even things that facilitate food preparation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source text for the dispute mentioned in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The existence and content of the dispute referred to in step 8.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת אֶלָּא אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ.

steps.title: What is the reason of the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the תנא קמא, who forbids מכשירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the first תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the תנא קמא gets his view that preparatory steps are forbidden. This sets up the next step, where the פסוק is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a source in the פסוק, not just the rule itself. It will look for the reason behind each side in turn.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (anonymous) opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural basis of the first opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source of the תנא קמא for forbidding מכשירי אוכל נפש.

steps.title: The word "הוא": only food itself, not its preparatory steps
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "הוא לבדו יעשה לכם". The word "הוא" teaches that only the food work itself is allowed, not its מכשירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "That alone may be done for you." "That" is allowed, but not the things that prepare for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing the פסוק that limits what is allowed on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "הוא" ("that") together with "לבדו" ("alone") is read as a limiting word. It narrows the permission to work done to the food itself, so tool repair is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: "That alone may be done for you" (שמות יב:טז)

phrases.english: The verse states:
"That alone may be done for you."
"That" — but not its facilitators.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: הוּא לְבַדּוֹ יֵעָשֶׂה לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "הוא" limits the permission to the food work itself, excluding מכשירין.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source: "לכם" means for all your needs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from "לכם" that everything you need for the meal is permitted, including מכשירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה: the פסוק says "for you," meaning for all your needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי יהודה's source from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads "לכם" as a widening word. Anything you need in order to eat, such as a working knife, counts as something done "for you."

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda: the verse states "for you,"
"for you" — for all your needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side's source, parallel to step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "לכם" widens the permission to all needs of the meal, including מכשירין.

steps.title: What does the תנא קמא do with "לכם"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא: the word "לכם" is also written, so how does he deal with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first תנא, isn't "for you" written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא to explain the word that רבי יהודה relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "לכם" means "all your needs," the תנא קמא seems to be ignoring a word in the פסוק. He has to give "לכם" a different job.

phrases.english: And the first tanna — isn't "for you" written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's word from step 12 against the תנא קמא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's reading in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק includes "לכם", which seems to widen the permission. The תנא קמא must account for it.

steps.title: "לכם" excludes cooking for non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא explains that "לכם" means for you, not for non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: that "for you" means for you, and not for non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא קמא answers by giving "לכם" a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, "לכם" is not a widening word but a narrowing one. It teaches that cooking on יום טוב is permitted only for Jews, not for גוים. That leaves no source for permitting מכשירין.
steps.confusionAlert: Here "לכם" is read by the תנא קמא as limiting (only for you), the exact opposite of how רבי יהודה reads it (for all your needs).

phrases.english: He would say to you: that "for you" —
and not for gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the word to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "לכם" must mean all your needs, so the תנא קמא seems to ignore it.
steps.terutzMaskana: "לכם" teaches that the permission is for Jews and not for non-Jews.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with "הוא"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: the limiting word "הוא" is also written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too, isn't "that" written?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the same challenge on רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה permits all מכשירין, he seems to ignore the limiting word "הוא". He also needs to account for it.

phrases.english: And the other one too — isn't "that" written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 13, now aimed at רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק includes the limiting word "הוא", which seems to exclude מכשירין.

steps.title: Both words apply: preparatory steps possible before יום טוב versus impossible
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses both words. "הוא" forbids מכשירין that could have been done on ערב יום טוב, and "לכם" permits those that could not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: "that" is written and "for you" is written, and there is no contradiction. One refers to preparatory steps that could be done before יום טוב, and the other refers to preparatory steps that could not be done before יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה resolves the challenge by dividing מכשירין into two groups, so that each word of the פסוק covers one group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not permit all מכשירין. If a step could have been done on ערב יום טוב, "הוא" forbids it on יום טוב. If it could not be done earlier, such as a knife that got nicked on יום טוב itself, "לכם" permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
Here (in one case)... there (in another case)
From the day before יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא forbids all מכשירי אוכל נפש on יום טוב, based on "הוא". רבי יהודה permits them only when they could not have been done before יום טוב, based on "לכם", while "הוא" still forbids those that could have been done earlier. This is why a knife that got nicked on יום טוב itself is the classic case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction, whether something could have been prepared before יום טוב, shapes how later rulings treat fixing tools on יום טוב.

phrases.english: He would say to you: "that" is written, and "for you" is written,
and it is not difficult:
here, regarding facilitators that it is possible
to do on the eve of the Festival;
there, regarding facilitators that it is impossible
to do on the eve of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: כְּתִיב הוּא, וּכְתִיב לָכֶם, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by dividing the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה ignores "הוא" and permits all מכשירין.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה permits only מכשירין that could not have been done before יום טוב. Those that could have been done earlier are forbidden by "הוא".
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי יהודה, both words of the פסוק work together, split by whether the preparatory step could have been done on ערב יום טוב.

steps.title: A bent skewer may not be fixed on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a roasting skewer that got bent may not be straightened on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A roasting skewer that became bent may not be fixed on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל: you may not straighten a bent skewer on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straightening a bent (נרצף) skewer counts as fixing a utensil (תיקון כלי). That is forbidden on יום טוב even though the skewer will be used for food. This is different from the crushed (נרצם) skewer in step 8, which depends on the מכשירין dispute; the next step's פשיטא shows this case seemed clearly forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A metal roasting skewer or spit
To fix it or repair it

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even where מכשירין may be permitted, actually repairing a utensil (תיקון כלי) is still forbidden on יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A skewer that became bent —
it is forbidden to fix it on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of rulings about skewers. The topic connects to the מכשירין discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bent skewer may not be straightened on יום טוב.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל needed to say this, since fixing a utensil on יום טוב is clearly forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone already knows you may not repair a utensil on יום טוב. So why would שמואל bother teaching it? The גמרא expects that the ruling must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. This is a challenge saying the ruling teaches nothing new.

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just stated in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling forbidding fixing a bent skewer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fixing utensils on יום טוב is already known to be forbidden, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Forbidden even when it can be straightened by hand
steps.stepSummary: The ruling teaches that fixing the skewer is forbidden even when no tool is needed and it can be bent back by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed: even though it can be straightened by hand, it is still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל's ruling adds something new: it is forbidden even when it is easy to fix by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought that a simple fix by hand, with no tools, is not real 'fixing.' שמואל teaches that it is still forbidden. Making the skewer usable again is what counts, not how hard the work is.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for this case. This phrase introduces the special case that makes the ruling new.
It can be straightened with one's hands

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem is using tools. Even with bare hands, straightening the skewer is forbidden.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary,
for even though it can be straightened by hand, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing to a new case (לא צריכא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A simple fix by hand would not count as fixing a utensil.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even straightening by hand counts as fixing and is forbidden.

steps.title: A used skewer may not be moved on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a skewer that was already used to roast meat may not be moved on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A skewer on which meat was roasted may not be moved on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling from שמואל: once a skewer has been used for roasting, you may not move it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the meat is done, the skewer has finished its job for the day. It is dirty and has no other use, so it is מוקצה and may not be moved (טלטול).

keyTerms.meaning: To move it. This refers to the laws of carrying or handling objects (טלטול).

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A skewer on which they roasted meat —
it is forbidden to move it on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling about skewers. This one is about moving it, not fixing it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A skewer already used for roasting is מוקצה and may not be moved on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב מלכיו: slide it out and put it in a corner
steps.stepSummary: רב מלכיו allows pulling the skewer out and placing it in a corner so nobody gets hurt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of רב מלכיו: He may pull it out and put it in a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מלכיו gives a limited permission: you may pull the skewer out and set it in a corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sharp skewer left in the middle of the house could injure someone. So even though it is normally not to be moved, he may pull it out of the meat and move it out of the way to a corner.

keyTerms.meaning: He slides it out or pulls it out

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav Malkiyu said:
He pulls it out and places it in a corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a safety exception to שמואל's ban on moving the skewer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may pull the used skewer out and put it in a corner.

steps.title: רב הונא: only when an olive-bulk of meat is on it
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits רב מלכיו's permission to a skewer that still has a כזית of meat on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב הונא: This is only when there is a כזית of meat on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא narrows רב מלכיו's permission. You may move the skewer only if a כזית of meat is still on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If meat is still on the skewer, the meat (which is allowed to be handled) gives a reason to move the skewer along with it. Without that meat, the skewer is plain מוקצה and may not be moved at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is only when. This phrase adds a limiting condition.
An olive-bulk, a standard halachic measure

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Ashi said that Rav Huna said:
And this is only when there is an olive-bulk of meat on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts a limit on רב מלכיו's permission from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Moving the skewer to a corner is allowed only if a כזית of meat remains on it.

steps.title: רבינא: allowed even without meat, like a thorn in the street
steps.stepSummary: רבינא disagrees and allows moving the skewer even with no meat on it, comparing it to removing a thorn from רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Even if there is no meat on it, it may be moved, just like a thorn in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא argues on רב הונא. He says you may move the skewer to the corner even with no meat on it, because of the danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא compares the skewer to a thorn lying in רשות הרבים. The רבנן allowed moving that thorn on שבת so people would not get hurt. The same safety reason lets us move the dangerous skewer, even with no meat to justify it.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like. This phrase introduces a comparison to a known case.

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on moving a used skewer. רב הונא says it is allowed only with a כזית of meat on it. רבינא says it is allowed even without meat, because of safety, like a thorn in the street.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that preventing harm to people can override the usual מוקצה restrictions.

phrases.english: Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו בָּשָׂר —
phrases.english: Even though there is no meat on it —
it is permitted to move it,
just as is the case with a thorn in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues on רב הונא's limitation in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The skewer may be moved to a corner even with no meat on it, for safety.

steps.title: Three rulings that belong to רב מלכיו
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בריה דרב איקא lists three rulings said by רב מלכיו: skewer, maidservants, and follicles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בריה דרב איקא said: The rulings of skewer, maidservants, and follicles were said by רב מלכיו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a side note. Since רב מלכיו was just mentioned, the גמרא lists which rulings in ש״ס are his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a few rulings are said in the name of רב מלכיו, so the גמרא gives a memory list. The skewer ruling is ours. 'Maidservants' is the rule in כתובות that a wife with many maidservants must still do some work. 'Follicles' is the rule that two hair follicles mark a girl as an adult.

keyTerms.meaning: Hair follicles, pits in the skin where hair grows

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new law about skewers. It is only a memory list saying who said which rulings.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chinena son of Rav Ika said:
Skewer, maidservants, and follicles —
are the rulings of Rav Malkiyu.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side note set off by the mention of רב מלכיו in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rulings on skewer, maidservants, and follicles are attributed to רב מלכיו.

steps.title: Three other rulings belong to רב מלכיא
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בריה דרב איקא continues: the rulings about the forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese were said by a different חכם, רב מלכיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese were said by רב מלכיא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of רב חיננא's statement from the previous step. After listing three rulings of רב מלכיו, he now lists three rulings that belong to a different חכם with a very similar name, רב מלכיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two names look almost the same, people could mix up who said what. רב חיננא gives a clear list: skewer, maidservants, and follicles belong to רב מלכיו, while forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese belong to רב מלכיא. The rulings themselves come from other places in ש״ס (for example, laws about cutting a non-Jew's hair, putting ashes on a wound, and non-Jewish cheese).

keyTerms.meaning: Forelock, a lock of hair grown for idol worship. A Jew cutting a non-Jew's hair must stop before reaching it.
Burnt ashes. One may not put them on a wound because the mark looks like a tattoo (כְּתֹבֶת קַעֲקַע).
Cheese. Non-Jewish cheese is forbidden, partly because its surface was smoothed with pig fat.
A different אמורא from רב מלכיו, with a very similar name.

steps.confusionAlert: רב מלכיא and רב מלכיו are two different people. Read the last letters carefully: ־יָא versus ־יוֹ.

phrases.english: Forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese
phrases.notes: Three rulings found elsewhere in ש״ס.

phrases.english: were said by Rav Malkiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּלוֹרִית, אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה, וּגְבִינָה — רַב מַלְכִּיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חיננא's list from step 24 by naming the rulings that belong to the other חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese belong to רב מלכיא, not רב מלכיו.

steps.title: רב פפא sorts the rulings by type
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that comments on a משנה or ברייתא come from רב מלכיא, and independent rulings come from רב מלכיו. His memory aid is 'the משנה is a queen' (מלכתא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: rulings on a משנה or a ברייתא are from רב מלכיא. Independent rulings are from רב מלכיו. Your memory aid: 'the משנה is a queen.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different way to sort the rulings between the two חכמים. Instead of a fixed list, he uses a rule based on what kind of teaching it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a ruling explains or comments on a משנה or ברייתא, it belongs to רב מלכיא. If it stands on its own (a שמעתתא), it belongs to רב מלכיו. The memory aid works because מַלְכְּתָא ('queen') sounds like מלכיא, and the משנה is the 'queen' of Torah texts.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that was left out of the משנה
Independent rulings of the אמוראים, not based on a משנה

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Rulings on a Mishnah or a baraita were said by Rav Malkiya.
phrases.notes: Comments tied to a תנאי source.

phrases.english: Independent rulings were said by Rav Malkiyu.
And your memory aid: the Mishnah is a queen.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מַתְנִיתִין וּמַתְנִיתָא — רַב מַלְכִּיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different system from רב חיננא's for deciding which חכם said which ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comments on a משנה or ברייתא belong to רב מלכיא. Independent rulings belong to רב מלכיו.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two systems?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רב חיננא's list and רב פפא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the two ways of sorting actually give different answers. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two systems mostly agree on who said what. The גמרא wants to find the specific ruling that one system gives to רב מלכיו and the other gives to רב מלכיא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is between them?': what practical difference is there between the two opinions

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רב חיננא's list with רב פפא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling is assigned to a different חכם by each of the two systems.

steps.title: The difference is the maidservants ruling
steps.stepSummary: The two systems differ on the maidservants ruling. רב חיננא gives it to רב מלכיו, while רב פפא gives it to רב מלכיא because it comments on a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them regarding maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two systems disagree about who said the ruling on maidservants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב חיננא's list, the maidservants ruling belongs to רב מלכיו. But that ruling comments on a dispute in a משנה, so by רב פפא's rule it belongs to רב מלכיא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is between them': the practical difference is

steps.whatToRemember: There are two systems for telling רב מלכיא and רב מלכיו apart: רב חיננא's fixed list, and רב פפא's rule (משנה-based = מלכיא, independent = מלכיו). They differ only on the maidservants ruling.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them regarding maidservants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The maidservants ruling: רב מלכיו according to רב חיננא, רב מלכיא according to רב פפא.

steps.title: No asking a butcher for a set price's worth of meat on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: on יום טוב a person may not say to a butcher 'weigh me a דינר's worth of meat.' But the butcher may slaughter an animal and divide it among the customers.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person should not say to a butcher: 'Weigh me a דינר's worth of meat.' But he slaughters and divides it among them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what you may and may not say when getting meat from a butcher on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming a price and a weight sounds like ordinary buying and selling, which is not allowed on יום טוב. Getting meat itself is fine: the butcher may slaughter and divide the animal among the people, as long as no price or measure is mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin of a set value

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not forbid getting meat from a butcher on יום טוב. It only forbids talking in business terms, such as naming a price or weight.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
A person may not say to a butcher:
'Weigh for me a dinar's worth of meat,'
phrases.notes: This sounds like a business deal.

phrases.english: but he slaughters and divides it among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַטַּבָּח: שְׁקוֹל לִי בְּדִינָר בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion about רב מלכיא and רב מלכיו ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not name a price or weight to the butcher, but the butcher may slaughter and divide the meat among the customers.

steps.title: How does one get meat in practice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a person can actually take his share of meat if he may not mention a price. It begins its answer with 'like this case,' and the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: How does he do it? Like this case...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the משנה. The words 'כי הא' set up the answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows dividing the meat but forbids naming a price. So the גמרא asks what method a person should use to get his share. It is about to answer with a story or example.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this, introducing an example or story

phrases.english: GEMARA:
How does one do it?
Like this case...
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to apply the rule from the משנה in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical method for taking a share of meat on יום טוב without naming a price.
